genesis.26.p1.b1.text: Now there was another famine in the land, subsequent to the one that had occurred in Abraham’s time. And Isaac went to Abimelech king of the Philistines at Gerar.

genesis.26.p1.b2.text: Do not go down to Egypt. Settle in the land where I tell you.

genesis.26.p1.b3.text: Stay in this land as a foreigner, and I will be with you and bless you. …

genesis.26.p1.b4.text: I will make your descendants as numerous as the stars in the sky, … and through your offspring all nations of the earth will be blessed,

genesis.26.p2.b7.text: When Isaac had been there a long time, Abimelech king of the Philistines looked down from the window and was surprised to see Isaac caressing his wife Rebekah.

genesis.26.p2.b8.text: So she is really your wife! How could you say, ‘She is my sister’?

genesis.26.p3.b9.text: Whoever harms this man or his wife will surely be put to death.

genesis.26.p3.b10.text: Now Isaac sowed seed in the land, and that very year he reaped a hundredfold. And the LORD blessed him, and he became richer and richer, until he was exceedingly wealthy.

genesis.26.p3.b11.text: the Philistines envied him. So the Philistines took dirt and stopped up all the wells that his father’s servants had dug in the days of his father Abraham.

genesis.26.p3.b12.text: Depart from us, for you are much too powerful for us.

genesis.26.p4.b13.text: So Isaac left that place and encamped in the Valley of Gerar and settled there.

genesis.26.p4.b14.text: Isaac reopened the wells … And he gave these wells the same names his father had given them.

genesis.26.p4.b16.text: So he named the well Esek, because they contended with him. Then they dug another well and quarreled over that one also; so he named it Sitnah.

genesis.26.p5.b17.text: He moved on from there and dug another well, and they did not quarrel over it. He named it Rehoboth

genesis.26.p5.b18.text: At last the LORD has made room for us, and we will be fruitful in the land.

genesis.26.p5.b19.text: From there Isaac went up to Beersheba,

genesis.26.p5.b20.text: I am the God of your father Abraham. Do not be afraid, for I am with you. …

genesis.26.p6.b21.text: Later, Abimelech came to Isaac from Gerar, with Ahuzzath his adviser and Phicol the commander of his army.

genesis.26.p6.b22.text: Why have you come to me? … You hated me and sent me away.

genesis.26.p6.b23.text: We can plainly see that the LORD has been with you, … We recommend that there should now be an oath between us and you. Let us make a covenant with you

genesis.26.p6.b24.text: … sending you on your way in peace. And now you are blessed by the LORD.

genesis.26.p7.b25.text: So Isaac prepared a feast for them, and they ate and drank.

genesis.26.p7.b26.text: And they got up early the next morning and swore an oath to each other. Then Isaac sent them on their way, and they left him in peace.

genesis.26.p7.b28.text: So he called it Shibah, and to this day the name of the city is Beersheba.

genesis.26.p8.b29.text: When Esau was forty years old, he took as his wives Judith daughter of Beeri the Hittite and Basemath daughter of Elon the Hittite.

genesis.26.p8.b30.text: And they brought grief to Isaac and Rebekah.
